sections.content: Impersonal se lets a text define a term, describe a widespread practice, or note an ongoing debate without naming a specific subject — exactly what's needed for something as informally recognized as caudillo authority. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Se llamaba caudillo a un líder regional cuya autoridad se apoyaba en su capacidad militar personal y su carisma.
items.english: A regional leader whose authority rested on personal military capacity and charisma was called a caudillo.

items.spanish: En muchas regiones, se reconocía su autoridad de facto mucho antes de que ningún cargo oficial la confirmara.
items.english: In many regions, his authority was recognized de facto long before any official post confirmed it.

items.spanish: Se exigía, en la vida cotidiana, el uso de una cinta roja como muestra pública de lealtad.
items.english: In everyday life, wearing a red ribbon was required as a public show of loyalty.

items.spanish: Se debate todavía, entre historiadores, si Rosas debe entenderse como un tirano o como un garante de orden.
items.english: It's still debated among historians whether Rosas should be understood as a tyrant or as a guarantor of order.

sections.content: Se debate todavía is a useful pattern whenever a text wants to flag an open historical question rather than settle it — it signals "historians disagree," which is exactly the honest move to make about a genuinely contested figure like Rosas.
